title: Database access with SQLAlchemy

spans.text: FastAPI builds JSON APIs that web and mobile applications call over HTTP; type annotations help validate inputs and describe the API contract.

SQLAlchemy ORM maps Python objects to SQL tables. This example uses its synchronous 2.x API and local SQLite: a model describes the table, a session manages a transaction, and a dependency opens/closes a session per request. Install with
pip install fastapi uvicorn httpx sqlalchemy

spans.code:
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict
from sqlalchemy import String, create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, Session, mapped_column, sessionmaker

engine = create_engine("sqlite:///./users.db", connect_args={"check_same_thread": False})
SessionLocal = sessionmaker(bind=engine)

class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass

class User(Base):
    __tablename__ = "users"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(80))

Base.metadata.create_all(engine)

class UserIn(BaseModel):
    name: str

class UserOut(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)
    id: int
    name: str

app = FastAPI()

def get_db():
    with SessionLocal() as session:
        yield session

@app.post("/users", response_model=UserOut)
def create_user(data: UserIn, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    user = User(name=data.name)
    db.add(user)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(user)
    return UserOut(id=user.id, name=user.name)

Request: POST /users  body={"name":"Ada"}; sonra GET /users/1
Response: The first call returns 200 JSON `{id:1,name:Ada}`; SQLite stores it for a later request.

from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict
from sqlalchemy import String, create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, Session, mapped_column, sessionmaker

engine = create_engine("sqlite:///./users.db", connect_args={"check_same_thread": False})
SessionLocal = sessionmaker(bind=engine)

class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass

class User(Base):
    __tablename__ = "users"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(80))

Base.metadata.create_all(engine)

class UserIn(BaseModel):
    name: str

class UserOut(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)
    id: int
    name: str

app = FastAPI()

def get_db():
    with SessionLocal() as session:
        yield session

@app.post("/users", response_model=UserOut)
def create_user(data: UserIn, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    user = User(name=data.name)
    db.add(user)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(user)
    return UserOut(id=user.id, name=user.name)

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

with TestClient(app) as client:
    response = client.post("/users", json={"name": "Ada"})
    print(response.status_code, response.json()["name"])

spans.title: Practical tip
spans.text: Close the session in `finally` after `yield`; override `get_db` with a test database in tests.

spans.title: One level deeper
spans.text: SQLite fits learning and small local apps; high-write or multi-server systems may need a database server and migrations.

spans.title: Important warning
spans.text: Plan backups and storage for SQLite in production; running `create_all` per request is not a schema migration strategy.
